verdict.rationale: Whether a product's source is available under an open license is a fair question for a SaaS meeting-transcription tool, so this axis applies. Nothing in the evidence pack shows Otter.ai publishing its source code or using an open license. The materials describe a proprietary cloud service with a public API, webhooks and an MCP server, none of which amount to open-source code.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
